2. Resources, connections and symbols

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-02-connect.Rmd
book-02-connect.Rmd

What you will learn

Distinguish a connection, a resource and a symbol, and change databases deliberately.

You need: the client packages and the Opal login from Getting started. This chapter uses omop.gibleed and omop.synthea.

Start this chapter 

library(dsOMOPClient)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.gibleed", server = "site")$conns

Three names with different jobs

A connection is a logged-in DataSHIELD session. A resource describes how the server opens a database. A symbol is an object name in that session. Here site names the connection, omop.gibleed selects the resource and omop names the attached database handle.

DSI::datashield.symbols(conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "omop"

Under site, omop is the private handle that ds.omop.login() created. Later, D_people will name a table created by a recipe, rather than a database handle.

Use a handle explicitly 

ds.omop.table.stats("person", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)
#> <dsomop_result>
#> Servers: site
#> Scope: per_site
#>
#> $site
#> $rows
#> [1] 2690
#>
#> $persons
#> [1] 2690

The request goes to GiBleed through omop: its person count is in the 2,690–2,694 band. Most dsOMOP calls default to symbol = "omop", so you can omit it when you have just one attached database. ds.omop.server.version() is different: it reports the server’s installed and available methods, independently of any database handle.

Switch resources

Release the attached resource, then attach another one through the same login:

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop.synthea", conns = conns)
ds.omop.table.stats("person", conns = conns)
#> <dsomop_result>
#> Servers: site
#> Scope: per_site
#>
#> $site
#> $rows
#> [1] 25
#>
#> $persons
#> [1] 25

The person band is now 25–29, containing Synthea27Nj’s 28 people. The handle is still called omop even though its database changed. Switching does not combine the two populations.

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop.gibleed", conns = conns)
ds.omop.table.stats("person", conns = conns)
#> <dsomop_result>
#> Servers: site
#> Scope: per_site
#>
#> $site
#> $rows
#> [1] 2690
#>
#> $persons
#> [1] 2690

The 2,690–2,694 band confirms that GiBleed is attached again. Choosing the resource explicitly prevents running a lab analysis against its empty numeric fields.

Exercise 1: keep two handles in one session

Attach omop.synthea as labs, keeping omop attached to GiBleed. List the names and count people through each. Does attaching labs combine them?

Solution

ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop.synthea", symbol = "labs", conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.symbols(conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "labs" "omop"

labs and omop are two distinct handles in the same session.

ds.omop.table.stats("person", stats = "persons", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)
#> <dsomop_result>
#> Servers: site
#> Scope: per_site
#>
#> $site
#> $persons
#> [1] 2690
ds.omop.table.stats("person", stats = "persons", symbol = "labs", conns = conns)
#> <dsomop_result>
#> Servers: site
#> Scope: per_site
#>
#> $site
#> $persons
#> [1] 25
ds.omop.disconnect(symbol = "labs", conns = conns)

omop gives 2690 and labs gives 25. Each is a separate protected count; the populations were not combined. Disconnecting labs leaves omop available.

Exercise 2: diagnose a wrong name

Ask for a person count through missing_handle. What needs fixing: the table name or the handle name?

Solution

ds.omop.table.stats("person", symbol = "missing_handle", conns = conns)
#> Error:
#> ! No OMOP session 'missing_handle'. Call ds.omop.connect() first.

The message identifies a missing session handle. It says nothing about whether the database has a person table. Use omop, or attach a resource under the name you intend to query.

End the session 

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(conns)

Disconnect releases the database handle; logout ends the DataSHIELD session. The next chapter logs in again.

Recap

A resource selects a database, a connection carries requests, and a symbol names a private server object. Check the selected resource before analysing it.
